 W.P.NO.128  THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA  WRIT PETITION NO: 12851/2025 O R D E R:
The present writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking following relief:
" ... to issue a direction, or an order, or a writ, more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondent Nos. 3 to 7 in marking the Desamsetti Appalanaidu vs The State Of Ap on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52112247/
1 properties of the petitioners, as shown in the Schedule appended to this petition, and interfering with such properties of the petitioners for the purpose of demolition in order to lay additional flyover by widening the road, which leads from north to south from Atchuthapuram Junction to Special Economic Zone, situated in Atchuthapuram Town of Atchuthapuram Mandal of Anakapalli District as illegal, arbitrary and violative of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India, and consequently to direct the Respondent Nos.3 to 7 not to interfere with the possession and enjoyment of the properties of the petitioners without following due process of law as contemplated under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, and to pass such..."(in verbatim)

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Revenue for the respondents.
3.

During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioners, without touching the merits of the case,
requested this Court to issue a direction to the respondents not to dispossess/evict the petitioners from their respective property without following due process of law.

4. Learned Government Pleader for Revenue submits that, if the petitioners are in possession of the subject property, the respondents would follow due process of law and requested to pass appropriate orders.
NV, J W.P.NO.12851 OF 2025 5.

When the petitioners are in settled possession and enjoyment of the property, the petitioners cannot be dispossessed, without following due process of law in view of the law declared by the Apex Court in "Rame Gowda (dead) by L.Rs. v. M.Varadappa Naidu (Dead) by L.Rs.1".

entities.text: L.Rs. v. M.Varadappa Naidu (Dead) by L.Rs.1"
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, if the petitioners are in possession of the subject property, the respondents are directed not to evict/dispossess the petitioners from the subject property, except by due process of law.
6. With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed of at the stage of admission with the consent of both the counsel.
Consequently, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall also stand closed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
